I got through all four steps, with three problems. My guessed Pen Pivot address gave a 404 at first, but I found the real page. On 10015.io, my first "Convert" click hit a "Case Converter" link and set off a full-screen ad. And I can't see bold text through my tools, so I couldn't check the bolding myself.

**1. Bing: "Latent Growth Models" (top three main results; the search tab is still open)**
1. **Latent growth modeling – Wikipedia** (en.wikipedia.org): a short overview of the method as part of structural equation modeling (SEM). It covers background, how change and differences between people are modeled, more complex growth shapes, and which software you can use.
2. **Estimating and visualizing Latent Growth Models with R** (longitudinalanalysis.com): a hands-on tutorial in R (using lavaan) with income data over six survey waves. It walks through the model's formula and how to plot change.
3. **Latent Growth Model – an overview | ScienceDirect Topics** (sciencedirect.com): short excerpts from academic book chapters, including latent class growth models and two-variable growth curve models with diagrams.

Each of these is open in its own tab.

**2. Google: outline prompt template.** The page I used is "ChatGPT Turns Messy Notes Into Organized Outlines" from The Pen Pivot (penpivot.com/p/chatgpt-transforms-notes, left open). It shows the full prompt, copied exactly:

> "Hi, ChatGPT. Let's work together to convert my jumbled notes into structured and organized notes. Please use the following information to help you create a more coherent and easy-to-understand version of my notes:
>
> Main purpose of the notes: [e.g. for an article/blog post, a book idea, for studying, as a reference, or for a presentation]
>
> Desired format for organized notes: [e.g. bullet points, numbered list, outline, mind map, or paragraphs]
>
> Target audience: [insert, if applicable]
>
> Priority topics or themes (optional): [insert any topics or themes that should be prioritized in the organized notes]
>
> Additional context or background (optional): [anything else that may help in organizing the notes]
>
> Here are the original notes:
>
> [Copy and paste original notes]

(The page doesn't have a closing quotation mark.) Google's AI Overview showed a different "Act as an expert research and content organizer…" version, but I couldn't find it on the page itself, so I left it out.

**3. 10015.io Bionic Reading Converter (tab left open)**
I typed your exact note and reloaded the page to clear the ad. The text now shows in both the input box and the "Bionic Reading Mode" results box at the default "Medium – 50%" setting. The tool works by bolding the first part of each word, but I couldn't check the bolding, so please look at the tab to confirm. If it isn't bold, click the "Convert" button under the text box. Here is my own version of the same style, not copied from the tool:

**Lat**ent **gro**wth **mod**els **ar**e **statis**tical **meth**ods **us**ed **t**o **esti**mate **cha**nge **ov**er **ti**me **acr**oss **indiv**iduals. **Th**ey **he**lp **resea**rchers **unde**rstand **traje**ctories, **diffe**rences **i**n **gro**wth, **an**d **predi**ctors **o**f **cha**nge.

**4. Bing: free plagiarism checker (Duplichecker, tab left open)**
I skipped Bing's sponsored results and picked **Duplichecker** (duplichecker.com), a regular result. The page is live, with a text box (limit 0 / 10,000 characters) and a **Check Plagiarism** button. To check your note:
1. Paste the note into the text box under "Paste" (it's only about 190 characters).
2. Click **Check Plagiarism**.
3. Read the result: it shows what percent is unique and what percent is plagiarized, and marks duplicate sentences in pink.

Your first sentence is worded a lot like the Wikipedia and ScienceDirect definitions ("growth trajectory of individuals over time"). If it gets flagged, reword it or add a citation before you share it.

**Open tabs:** Bing results, the three result pages, Pen Pivot, 10015.io and Duplichecker. I closed the Google search results tab to stay under the browser's tab limit, and the Bing plagiarism search is also still open.
